title: Quality Studio named rule
description: A single named best-practice rule stored file-first under rules/<technology>/<id>.json. One file per rule; the file's git history is the rule's change history in addition to the changelog array.

id.description: Stable rule id. Never reused once shipped; a retired rule is marked deprecated instead of deleted or renumbered.

technology.description: The primary technology the rule applies to. Extend the enum, don't overload an existing value, when a new seed set is added.

category.description: Grouping used for seed-set coverage and browsing, e.g. 'design-tokens' or 'async-hygiene'.

statement.description: The one- or two-sentence rule itself, phrased as a directive. This is what a reviewer cites.

rationale.description: Why the rule exists: the failure mode it prevents or the property it protects.

severity.description: Default severity when the rule fires. Matches the finding envelope's severity enum (schemas/quality-finding.v1.schema.json).

autofixable.description: Whether a mechanical fix exists that a coding agent (or codemod) can apply without design judgement.

defaultOn.description: Whether this rule belongs to the core that InputResolver supplies automatically to every project unless .quality/rules.config.json overrides it.

kinds.description: Review kinds the rule participates in.

levels.description: Review hierarchy levels the rule applies at.

version.description: Semver of this rule's content. Bump on any statement, severity, or example change.

supersededBy.description: Rule id that replaces this one. Required when status is deprecated.

changelog.description: Append-only history of substantive changes to this rule, newest first.

then.description: A deprecated rule must name the rule that replaces it, so an id is never retired into a dead end.

source.description: Repository-relative path the example was grounded in, when it is a real excerpt rather than illustrative.
